findings.detail: The first cut checked the new claim but let a second stale SessionFile view append from its own ordinal under the same owner. SessionFile now binds the file identity and size and refuses a view whose bytes changed.

The first cut attempted to bind a not-yet-created session in the claim constructor. Empty-session initialization now leaves identity unset until the header write and keeps that identity across appends.
The second review pass found symlink and hard-link aliases could bypass the path-local claim. Both aliases now fail closed before the target is read or changed.

The first exact-SHA CI matrix exposed that a replaced session could reuse the same inode, so dev+ino alone did not detect it on Linux. SessionFile now holds the original descriptor and compares fstat with the current path lstat before append.

The second exact-SHA CI run showed Windows could not delete temporary session directories while the replacement guard held a read descriptor. POSIX keeps the descriptor for an open-file race check; Windows opens only long enough to read platform identity and closes before returning.
